---
title: "What I Built"
subtitle: "A training-time diagnostic that finds what other tools miss"
---

> **SART is a blood test for training data** — it finds which samples are teaching your model the wrong thing, then fixes the training in real-time.

---

## How It Works

SART is a training-time diagnostic and correction system for LLMs. It uses gradient signals to automatically detect which training samples teach shortcuts instead of reasoning — then fixes the training in real-time. No manual labeling, no retraining, no prior knowledge of what shortcuts exist.

```{dot}
//| label: fig-detect
//| fig-cap: "Step 1: Detect — which samples teach shortcuts?"
//| fig-width: 6
//| fig-height: 2.5
digraph G {
  bgcolor="transparent"
  rankdir=LR
  graph [ranksep=0.6, nodesep=0.5]
  node [style=filled, fillcolor="#2c3035", color="#4a9eda",
        fontcolor="#f8f9fa", fontname="Arial", fontsize=10,
        shape=box, width=2.0, height=0.5, margin="0.12,0.08"]
  edge [color="#6c757d", penwidth=1.4]

  Input [label="Training Batch\n+ Validation Set", fillcolor="#375a7f"]
  SS [label="ShortcutScore\nGradient-based\nper-sample metric"]
  Output [label="Shortcut Report\nEach sample scored", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]

  Input -> SS -> Output
}
```

```{dot}
//| label: fig-correct
//| fig-cap: "Step 2: Correct — two composable strategies"
//| fig-width: 6
//| fig-height: 3
digraph G {
  bgcolor="transparent"
  rankdir=TB
  graph [ranksep=0.45, nodesep=0.6]
  node [style=filled, fillcolor="#2c3035", color="#4a9eda",
        fontcolor="#f8f9fa", fontname="Arial", fontsize=10,
        shape=box, width=2.0, height=0.5, margin="0.12,0.08"]
  edge [color="#6c757d", penwidth=1.4]

  Score [label="ShortcutScore\nper-sample result", fillcolor="#375a7f"]
  RW [label="Sample Reweighting\nDown-weight bad samples", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]
  GS [label="Gradient Surgery\nRemove harmful signals", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]

  Score -> RW
  Score -> GS

  { rank=same; RW; GS }
}
```

## Why It's Different

```{dot}
//| label: fig-differentiators
//| fig-cap: "Three properties that no existing method combines"
//| fig-width: 6
//| fig-height: 2.5
digraph G {
  bgcolor="transparent"
  rankdir=LR
  graph [ranksep=0.5, nodesep=0.5]
  node [style=filled, fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c",
        fontcolor="#f8f9fa", fontname="Arial", fontsize=10,
        shape=box, width=2.0, height=0.55, margin="0.12,0.08"]
  edge [style=invis]

  A [label="Automatic\nNo prior knowledge\nof shortcut types"]
  B [label="Per-Sample\nPinpoints exact\nproblematic examples"]
  C [label="Single-Pass\nDetect + correct\nin one training run"]

  A -> B -> C
}
```

- **Automatic detection** — gradient signatures reveal shortcuts without human annotation
- **Per-sample granularity** — pinpoints exactly which training examples are problematic, not just which groups
- **Single-pass** — detects and corrects in one training run, unlike methods that require training twice

Benchmarked against 12 existing methods across 5 datasets — SART is the only approach that combines all three.

## Why This Can Be a Product

```{dot}
//| label: fig-product-path
//| fig-cap: "Incremental adoption — no all-or-nothing commitment"
//| fig-width: 6
//| fig-height: 3
digraph G {
  bgcolor="transparent"
  rankdir=TB
  graph [ranksep=0.45, nodesep=0.5]
  node [style=filled, fillcolor="#2c3035", color="#4a9eda",
        fontcolor="#f8f9fa", fontname="Arial", fontsize=10,
        shape=box, width=2.0, height=0.5, margin="0.12,0.08"]
  edge [color="#6c757d", penwidth=1.4]

  API [label="Diagnostic API\nStandalone value\nas shortcut report", fillcolor="#375a7f"]
  Correct [label="Add Correction\nReweighting + Surgery\nwhen ready", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]
  Integrate [label="Pipeline Callback\nZero migration cost\nplug into existing workflow", fillcolor="#1a4a3a", color="#00bc8c"]

  API -> Correct -> Integrate
}
```

- **The diagnostic output is independently valuable** — per-sample shortcut scores work as a standalone API
- **Composable adoption** — customers can start with diagnosis, add correction later
- **Zero migration cost** — the interface is a training callback, not a pipeline replacement
